title: A FRAMEWORK FOR STUDYING AI AGENT BEHAVIOR: EVIDENCE FROM CONSUMER CHOICE EXPERIMENTS

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring shifts in product choice probabilities when introducing psychological nudges (authority, social proof, scarcity, negative framing) and manipulating attributes (price, ratings) in a binary choice shopping task.
Analyzing the impact of the order in which products are presented (viewed first vs. second) on the agent's selection probability in a 2-alternative forced choice setting.
